initial_plan.answerability: partly: the data can compare pedestrian casualty burden per reported crash by crash time, but cannot measure pedestrian exposure or individual pedestrian risk
initial_plan.metric: (number_of_pedestrians_injured + number_of_pedestrians_killed) / included reported crashes * 100, shown as pedestrian casualties per 100 crashes
initial_plan.denominator: crashes with a usable date, a valid crash_time, and nonmissing values in both pedestrian outcome columns
initial_plan.population: police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crashes in all years represented by valid crash_date values
initial_plan.years: all years represented by valid crash_date values in the file
initial_plan.grouping: Night = crash_time from 20:00 through 05:59; day = 06:00 through 19:59

data_check_decisions.scope_change: Use only complete calendar years 2013-2025 so both time-of-day groups are compared over the same complete-year span; partial boundary years are excluded even though pedestrian outcomes are complete in 2026.
data_check_decisions.year_exclusions: Exclude 136,969 valid-date rows from partial 2012 and 2026 (6.036038% of all valid-date rows): 2012 covers only July 1-December 31 and 2026 only January 1-June 11.
data_check_decisions.outcome_missingness: Neither pedestrian outcome column has missing values among the 2,132,218 candidate rows in 2013-2025, so no in-range crashes are excluded for outcome missingness.
data_check_decisions.time_values: Keep all 23,787 rows in 2013-2025 with crash_time 00:00:00 because midnight is a valid time; disclose the possible default-time pile-up.
data_check_decisions.date_time_quality: There are no missing crash dates or times in the candidate rows used for these years, and no impossible nonmissing typed TIME values.

final_plan.answerability: partly: compares pedestrian casualty counts per reported crash by recorded crash time, but cannot measure pedestrian exposure or per-trip pedestrian risk
final_plan.metric: Sum of number_of_pedestrians_injured plus number_of_pedestrians_killed divided by included reported crashes, multiplied by 100; pedestrian casualties per 100 crashes
final_plan.denominator: 2,132,218 police-reported crashes with valid date/time and nonmissing pedestrian outcome values, during complete calendar years 2013-2025
final_plan.population: Police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crashes from 2013 through 2025, with a valid recorded crash time; pedestrian casualty counts are summed across all people involved
final_plan.limitations: This is pedestrian casualties per reported motor-vehicle crash, not pedestrian risk per crossing, trip, or amount of walking; pedestrian exposure is unavailable. Years are pooled without year adjustment. All 23,787 recorded-midnight crashes are retained although midnight may be a default-time pile-up. Partial 2012 and 2026 are excluded; file dates end 2026-06-11.
